Let tell you guys how I built my career to where it is today. With the help of one of the Production Coordinators for #BlackIsKing 😭😭🥰🥰 I had to put it in there! Thread:

So at my last job I was a captioner for an Australian company, captioning UK, US and Australian (and NZ) shows. Then I had the idea of caption in the SA industry, which I learned is subtitling. So I decided I was going to leave work and go transcribe and caption as a freelancer.

I left work end of Jan and started transcribing and doing admin to make a living until I decided to go into subtitling. I had contacted Tumi late last year to learn the ropes but never got to doing it. So when lockdown started, I contacted her and asked her to be my mentor.

We exchanged emails and got to discussing work and I was in!! I did a file for them and got paid for the very first time as a subtitler!🥳💃🏾 Weeks sown the line, I got a call from Tumi to say that I would be getting a call from my newest client (the big production company).

I kept on trabscribing while waiting for the call and to hear if my first client would be giving me more work. Lmao, I cried almost everyday asking a God for a job because this freelancing thing wasn’t working out.

Not even an hour later, I got an email asking if I’d be able to assist with subtitling a video. When I saw the company name, I nearly fell over!!😭😭 I sent everything they needed and I got a call and that’s how I landed my biggest client within four months of learning subtitling

Then on Thursday, my first client told me we’d be working together more and that I’m be getting more work from them. Friday morning, Tumi texted me to say I’m going to get a call from this production company.
9 years after my human’s passing and I still get shocked at how fresh the grief is when it visits.

I’ve updated my CV twice in the last week and I added ‘subtitler’ with my references and the latest one setting the mark for my career. I’m going to focus on my portfolio this month and for the rest of the year. Amaphupho a fezeka, izinto ziya hlangana. My heart is truly full!
